title: Ammon
lead: A people and kingdom east of the Jordan, around Rabbah (modern Amman). The Bible traces them to Lot and records long wars with Israel, from Jephthah and Saul to David and the prophets.

sections.b: Genesis traces the Ammonites to Lot's younger daughter (Genesis 19:38). Israel was told not to attack them (Deuteronomy 2:19), but they were barred from the assembly (Deuteronomy 23:3–4). Jephthah fought them (Judges 11), Saul's first victory was over Nahash the Ammonite at Jabesh-gilead (1 Samuel 11), and David took Rabbah (2 Samuel 12:26–31). Solomon married an Ammonite, Naamah, mother of Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:21), and built a shrine for Milcom, their god (1 Kings 11:5–7). The prophets announce Ammon's judgment (Amos 1:13–15; Jeremiah 49:1–6; Ezekiel 25:1–7). Ammonite inscriptions and the citadel of Amman show a settled kingdom by the ninth century BC.
